title: Follow a CloudFront request through cache and failure states
description: Switch scenarios to see where request processing runs, which cache layer answers, and when origin capacity or failover becomes user-visible.

nodes.label: Viewer
nodes.detail: A browser, app, or service connects to the distribution hostname and experiences the final latency, freshness, and authorization result.

nodes.label: Viewer function
nodes.detail: A CloudFront Function or viewer-request Lambda@Edge function can normalize the URI, query string, cookies, and headers before CloudFront identifies a cache object.

nodes.label: Edge cache
nodes.detail: Returns a reusable object immediately on a hit. On a miss, the request continues through CloudFront's cache hierarchy.

nodes.label: Regional cache
nodes.detail: Aggregates demand from multiple edge locations so a miss at one edge may still avoid the origin path.

nodes.label: Origin Shield
nodes.detail: Centralizes requests for an origin and can consolidate simultaneous misses for the same object before the origin.

nodes.label: Primary origin
nodes.detail: Generates or retrieves content. Its tested miss-path capacity remains a hard dependency for uncached traffic.

nodes.label: Failover origin
nodes.detail: Receives eligible requests only after the primary returns a status or failure configured for origin failover.

scenarios.label: Edge hit
scenarios.summary: The normalized cache key matches a fresh object at the nearest edge location.
scenarios.result: CloudFront returns the object without a regional-cache or origin request. Viewer-request logic still runs because it occurs before cache lookup.

scenarios.label: Regional hit
scenarios.summary: The nearest edge misses, but a regional cache already holds the object.
scenarios.result: The edge refills from CloudFront's cache hierarchy. The origin remains protected even though the nearest edge reported a miss.

scenarios.label: Shield miss burst
scenarios.summary: Several edges request the same uncached object. Origin Shield receives their misses and forwards a consolidated origin request.
scenarios.result: A centralized cache layer can reduce duplicate simultaneous origin work. Unique misses still reach the primary, so Origin Shield does not replace origin capacity planning.

scenarios.label: Origin failure
scenarios.summary: The primary returns a configured failover condition and CloudFront tries the secondary origin in its origin group.
scenarios.result: Only eligible requests and failure conditions follow this path. The secondary must have compatible content, authorization, and capacity before failover is useful.
